non_claims: These are statements about the toy model; they neither establish nor refute the corresponding claims about Rust, rustc or Miri. Model–system relation: none proved.

`CritCovers` and H1–H3 range over `positions P`: the source body and the shims in `reachableShims P`. That list over-approximates the shims a run enters (it ignores early termination), so a hypothesis can fail on a position no run executes; it contains no shim of a type the program never reaches.

No write-back to the original place is modelled. Staging without write-back preserves behaviour in the toy because a staged drop or free consumes the value and a staged clone reads it without writing; staging an operation that mutates a live place is outside the model.

Clone shims take a raw pointer and never observe addresses, and H2 constrains staged drops alone; an address-observing or interior-mutable `Clone` cannot be expressed. In Rust, `Clone::clone` takes `&self`; this card neither establishes nor refutes anything about staging such clones.
Aliasing raw pointers into the packed field during a staged operation, and unwinding or panics during staging or destruction, are not modelled.

A box's pointee is dropped at its heap address whatever the box's address, so staging a `Box<T>` field moves the pointer, not the pointee; H2 does not constrain pointees behind a box (`addrBlind_box_pos`, `staging_box_of_addrObs_pointee`).
The theorem does not assume acyclicity: it also covers runs that end with `outOfFuel`, and equality of observable traces does not imply that the runs complete.
`CritCovers` is a hypothesis; that `critType` meets it is `criterion-type-covers`.
`SafeSrc` is a sufficient syntactic restriction; programs with raw-pointer operations are covered by `sufficiency` for the `NoUB` part, and trace preservation for them is not stated.
Traces compare value names, not memory contents: the toy has no byte memory, so "the staged copy equals the original value" holds by construction, not by proof.

`NoUB` holds for runs with no misaligned reference creation and for runs ending with `trap`, `stuck` or `outOfFuel` before any UB event; it does not say that a run traps. That the instrumented run emits `trap` exactly where the uninstrumented run emits a UB event at a checked position is `precision`; combining the two, under a covering policy every UB event of the uninstrumented run becomes a trap.

The policy is fixed before the program and every program shares the body name `.src`, so the "only if" direction forces checks at every source position (including positions holding `readUnaligned` or `moveOut`) and in every existing shim kind of every type with alignment not 1 (including clone shims of types that need not be cloneable in Rust), because a client may call any existing shim and a `rawRef` may sit at any position. `FrameAligned` is not assumed. For a restricted class (no unsafe clients, or some shims never called) coverage of fewer operations can suffice (`sufficiency`).

Escape hatch — redundant checks: in richer shims with several reference creations, omitting a check whose misalignment always implies an earlier checked one can preserve completeness; the toy's shims have one reference creation (op 0), and every existing shim is directly callable, so this does not arise here (not proved for richer shims).

Escape hatch — caller-side checks: `srcStep` consults no check at `rawCall` sites, so checking a raw address at the call site before entering a shim is outside the policy space; this card neither establishes nor refutes the completeness of caller-side checking.
